title: Seasoned Beef Mince — Nachos & Tacos
description: The foundation of great nachos and tacos — a rich, deeply seasoned beef mince that holds its own under cheese, sour cream, and all the toppings. Works with a homemade seasoning blend or the Old El Paso packet. Builds fast and tastes like you spent hours on it.

ingredients.item: Taco Seasoning (see tacoseasoning recipe, or 1 × Old El Paso packet)

method.instruction: Dice the onion finely. Mince or finely chop the garlic.
Heat oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook 3–4 minutes until softened and starting to colour.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add beef mince. Break it up aggressively with a wooden spoon or spatula — you want fine crumbles, not chunks. Cook over high heat for 5–7 minutes until well browned. Don't rush this step; good colour on the mince means better flavour.
Drain off excess fat if needed — leave a little for flavour, not a pool of it.
Add tomato paste and stir through for 1–2 minutes until it darkens slightly and coats the mince.
Add taco seasoning (full batch of homemade or 1 packet Old El Paso) and stir through for 30 seconds.
Add canned crushed tomatoes. Stir well to combine. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has reduced and thickened and coats the mince well. It should not be watery — if it is, keep simmering.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. The mince should be bold and well-seasoned — it needs to hold up under all the nacho toppings.

notes.title: The Mince Matters
notes.content: Use beef mince at 80/20 fat ratio if you can find it — the extra fat carries the seasoning better and gives richer flavour. If your mince is very lean (90/10), add an extra tablespoon of oil when browning. Don't use extra-lean mince for this — it goes dry and gritty.

notes.title: Nacho Assembly
notes.content: Spread corn chips on an oven tray. Spoon mince generously over the top. Cover with grated cheese (tasty, cheddar, or a Mexican blend). Bake at 200°C for 8–10 minutes until cheese is melted and golden. Top with sour cream, guacamole, jalapeños, and fresh salsa to serve.

notes.title: Taco Assembly
notes.content: Warm taco shells in the oven for 5 minutes at 180°C. Fill generously with mince, then top with shredded lettuce, diced tomato, grated cheese, sour cream, and a squeeze of lime.

notes.title: Make It Go Further
notes.content: A drained 400 g can of kidney beans or black beans stirred in at step 8 stretches the mince to serve 6 and adds great texture and body. Classic Tex-Mex move.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: The beef mince reheats beautifully. Make a double batch, refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water to loosen it.
